note: ASCII-only: the accented letter is left alone where Emacs case-converts it. Built with char-to-string and reported as codepoints so the case file, the expression and the record are all ASCII -- the oracle shim's stdout is not UTF-8 for a multibyte string. capitalize additionally shows the word rule: a byte of a multi-byte character is a word constituent here, so the letters after it are not each read as the start of a word.
